title: The Hymns of the Atharvaveda
dateDisplay: c. 1200–800 BCE (with later material in Books XIX–XX)
attributionNote: The Atharvaveda is anonymous and composite. Its hymns are the work of the Atharvan and Angirasa priestly families, and Books XIX and XX contain later additions drawn partly from the Rigveda.
description: The Atharvaveda is the fourth Veda and the least liturgical of them: a collection of charms, exorcisms, prayers for health, prosperity and victory, speculative hymns on brahman, time and the primordial giant, and the great funeral and marriage rites. It preserves a side of Vedic religion that the Rigveda barely shows — the everyday fears and hopes of householders, and the specialist knowledge of the healing and sorcery priest.
historicalContext: The collection survives in the Saunaka and Paippalada recensions; Griffith translates the Saunaka text in twenty books. His two-volume translation of 1895–96 was the first complete English rendering and remains the standard public-domain one; the archive serves the twenty books as twenty pages.
availabilityNote: Complete. All twenty books of Griffith's translation are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one book per chapter. The volume's preface and errata are not part of the work.
